label: GO: choosing a1 after an unrewarded trial, early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO (never at D1 or D2), and almost only when the agent is about to pick a1 (98% of mass on model_act == 1). Within that, it needs the previous trial to have gone unrewarded (95% of mass on prev_reward == 0) and it is strongly tied to time in the episode: highest in trials 0-30, falling off through about trial 50 and silent after 60. Activation mass also sits in a narrow high band of the value head (7.73-8.10), which likely tracks episode time too. Predicate uses only the agent own policy argmax plus observed history (no future variables). Dev F1 0.59, mass recall 0.83, and it covers 93% of the top activation quartile. Precision is limited because many early unrewarded a1 GO steps stay silent, often after runs of unrewarded trials. Restricting to switching to a1 after an unrewarded non-a1 trial raises precision to 0.71 but halves recall. Nothing simple involving the hidden good state, transition type, or stay/switch improved F1.
